Perfect! After **Rb4+ Kf3 Rf4+ Kg3 Rxf7**, White has won the f7 pawn and has material advantage (White: 7+1=8 vs Black: 7).

**Best move: Rb4+**

**Main line:** Rb4+ Kf3 (if Black plays other moves like Kg5, Kg3, etc., White also has winning continuations) Rf4+ Kg3 Rxf7

**Motif: fork** (the rook on f4 attacks both the king on f3 and the undefended pawn on f7 simultaneously)

**Coaching note:**
When you see an opponent's king driven to an awkward square, look for a follow-up check that wins material. Here, Rb4+ forces the king forward, and after Kf3 Rf4+ is a fork—the rook attacks the king and an undefended piece simultaneously. The king must move, allowing you to capture the pawn. Always scan for this pattern: checks that set up tactics on the next move.
